title: WPMS/976/2020 of BHARAT SADHU SAMAJ SWARGASHRAM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 976 of 2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Brief Holder for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
According to the petitioner, a lease in
respect of land situate in Revenue Village
Jonk, Tehsil Yamkeshwar, District Pauri
Garhwal was granted to him under
Government Grants Act, in the year 1960.
Petitioner wants his leasehold right to be
converted into freehold right and for this
purpose, he has deposited the requisite fee
on 21.07.2014. Since no decision was
taken on petitioner's application, therefore,
petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking
following relief:
"(i) To issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus to direct respondent
no. 2 to complete the formalities and to
convert the lease land in favor of petitioner
as freehold land and to do all needful
including the execution of deed."
Learned counsel for the petitioner has
placed reliance upon Government Order
dated 01.03.2009 in support of his
contention that petitioner is entitled for
conversion of his leasehold right into
freehold right.
I have gone through the said
Government Order. The Government Order
deals only with Nazul land and provides
that subject to fulfillment of certain
conditions, the leasehold rights in respect
of Nazul land, can be converted into

freehold rights. It does not deal with lease
granted under Government Grants Act.
Nazul land is a separate category of
land which is governed by provisions
contained under Nazul Manual. It is owned
by the State Government and managed by
Urban Local Bodies, like Municipality.
Learned Brief Holder submits that
petitioner was never asked to deposit any
fee and whatever amount he has deposited
for conversion of leasehold rights to
freehold, was unauthorizedly deposited by
him on his own accord.
Petitioner himself has admitted in
paragraph no. 6 of the writ petition that he
was granted lease in respect of the land in
question under Government Grants Act. A
lease granted under Government Grants
Act cannot be converted into freehold land.
Moreover, the land in question was part of a
revenue village until five years ago as stated
by learned counsel for the petitioner and
Nazul land exists only in a municipality.
Since the subject land does not qualify
to be a Nazul land, therefore, the relief
sought in the writ petition cannot be
granted.
Even otherwise also, there can be no
direction to the State Government, which is
owner of the land, to sell out the subject
land in favour of the petitioner, by
executing a freehold deed.
Accordingly, the writ petition fails and
is dismissed.
